The Czech Republic is open to further discussions on additional passenger and cargo air connections with Kazakhstan, including possible routes involving Shymkent and, on the Czech side, Karlovy Vary, the Czech Ministry of Transport told Trend . The ministry welcomed the recent progress in air connectivity between the Czech Republic and Kazakhstan, including direct flights between Astana and Prague and the newly launched Almaty-Prague route operated by VietJet. "The Czech side is open to further discussions on additional passenger and cargo connections, including possible routes involving Shymkent and, on the Czech side, Karlovy Vary. Czech aviation stakeholders, including training institutions and companies active in air navigation and aviation technologies, are also ready to explore cooperation with Kazakh partners," the ministry said. The ministry noted that, building on the launch of the Czech Smart Mobility Ecosystem (Smart Mobility and Transportation Technology | Centrum dopravního výzkumu, v. v. i.), which brings together intelligent transport systems, transport research, Czech companies, academia and research institutions, the Czech Republic can offer comprehensive smart mobility solutions. These include intelligent transport systems, autonomous driving, transport digitalisation, safety and traffic management systems, logistics tools, and advanced solutions for road, rail and air navigation. The ministry said that Czech Minister of Transport Ivan Bednárik is scheduled to visit Kazakhstan as part of a broader business and scientific mission to Central Asia planned for October 11-16, 2026. "The mission aims to explore potential cooperation in this area with relevant stakeholders, including the city governments of Astana and Almaty and local integrators. We are also following the development of the National Digital Transport Platform for the real-time management of transport and logistics chains, which could create opportunities for experienced Czech companies to participate in this emerging ecosystem," the ministry said. Ranking the 11 best European cities for gay travelers by cost We're ranking these hot queer tourist destinations by how easy they are on your wallet. Ariel Messman-Rucker Nov 10, 2026 Ariel Messman-Rucker Ariel Messman-Rucker is an Oakland-born journalist who now calls the Pacific Northwest her home. When she’s not writing about politics and queer pop culture, she can be found reading, hiking, or talking about horror movies with the Zombie Grrlz Horror Podcast Network. For globe-trotting queer travelers, Europe is the perfect destination to explore. The continent is full of LGBTQ+ friendly cities with thriving nightlife scenes and vibrant gayborhoods . From Mykonos to Prague, you’ll be able to travel to find other queer people and exciting places to visit. But it can also be expensive. So we’ve gathered the data on the very best cities in Europe for LGBTQ+ travelers and then ranked them from most affordable to least. 11. Mykonos, Greece Mykonos, Greece fokkebok/Envato Mykonos is Europe’s most iconic and historic LGBTQ+ summer destinations and while it can be absurdly expensive to visit, it’s well worth the money. Not only are there stunning beaches, including Elia, which has a gay section and a clothing-optional area, but if you’re a gay circuit party lover, you can come for the week-long XLSIOR Festival where 30,00 gays descend on the island. 10. London, England London, England angelsantana/Envato London is one of the most expensive cities on the list, but it also has gay bars, nightclubs, and sex shops in a vibrant gayborhood in Soho and was found to have the best cruising scene in a 2025 study by Erobella , so while the city might not be cheap to stay in, you’ll definitely have a great time. 9. Amsterdam, Netherlands Amsterdam, Netherlands Dmitry_Rukhlenko/Envato Amsterdam is pricey, but it’s also a great destination for LGBTQ+ travelers. In fact, it’s a city you’ll want to visit more than once so that you can experience all of the cruising clubs, gay saunas, legendary queer parties and bars, and Canal Pride if you can get there in August. Check out the main LGBTQ+ area, Reguliersdwarsstraat, which has been thriving since the ’60s and still has plenty to offer queer travelers. 8. Paris, France Paris, France Chesnot/Getty Images The city of love has a thriving gay scene, world-renowned food, and a rich history to explore. Stay in the gay district of La Marais, where there are plenty of energetic gay clubs, nightclubs, and parties, and where you can get a phallic-shaped burger at Tata Burger and penis-shaped desserts at Legay Choc. And if you’re feeling uninhibited and horny, go to the local gay cruising spot Le Next while you’re in town. 7. Stockholm, Sweden Stockholm, Sweden Great_bru/Envato While more expensive than other options on this list, Stockholm is also considered one of the best cities for LGBTQ+ travelers for a reason. It’s one of those rare foreign destinations where you can be openly queer without having to look over your shoulder. The city doesn’t have a specific gayborhood, but you’ll find plenty of gay bars and nightclubs like Club Back Door, and you can take a walking tour of the LGBTQ+ history in the area. 6. Milan, Italy Milan, Italy Image Source/Envato Milan is not only the fashion capital of the world, but it’s one of the largest and best gay-friendly cities in Europe. Puerto Venezia is the gateway to the LGBTQ+ area in Milan, where. There you’ll find rainbows everywhere, plenty of gay bars like Leccomilano and the bear bar Company Club, and queer crowds spilling out into the streets. 5. Copenhagen, Denmark Copenhagen, Denmark High Fliers/Envato For LGBTQ+ travelers looks for a more tranquil and charming experience, Copenhagen is the perfect city to visit. You can watch your stress drift away as you explore the city’s picturesque canals, liberal social values, and thriving gay scene with some of the oldest gay bars in Europe. 4. Berlin, Germany Berlin, Germany AtlasComposer/Envato If you’re queer and haven’t made your way to Berlin, Germany yet, you’re missing out on one of the most LGBTQ+ friendly cities in the world. Travel to the Schöneberg district to visit Prinzknecht for one of the top cruising and fetish bars in this affordable city, where you’ll also find gay dance parties at Hafen and the gay dive bar Blond. And if you’re a history buff, you’ll be able to take guided walking tours of the areas that were historically full of queer folks. 3.. Lisbon, Portugal Lisbon, Portugal KSENIA7777/Envato Lisbon is a gorgeous and affordable city on Portugal’s coast that legalized gay marriage in 2010, five years before the U.S., so you can feel comfortable being yourself while checking out gay clubs, bars, and tourist hot spots. The city is truly an underrated hidden gem in Europe, with a vibrant gay scene in the Barrio Alto and Principe Real neighborhoods and the gay beach Praia 19 only 30 minutes away. 2. Madrid, Spain Madrid, Spain stockscar/Envato If you want a beach vacation and clubbing, head to Ibiza, but if you’re looking for an urban LGBTQ+ vibe full of gay bars, sex clubs, and Chueca, one of the best gayborhoods in Europe, then Madrid is the destination for you. It’s also home to Madrid Pride, which is so huge and vibrant that it has become ersatz Euro Pride. 1. Prague, Czech Republic Prague, Czech Republic dabobabo/Envato This picturesque city is full of art and architecture and is home to the annual Czech Republic’s Pride parade and Mezipatra Queer Film Festival. It’s also the most affordable option on the list, so if you’re on a budget, head there to check out the lively LGBTQ+ nightlife and the popular gayborhood, Vinohrady.
